items.title: Lawrence Marrero Interview, 1959-01-02
items.q: Also with Kid René. Bill I played most every band in the city.

ctx.x: Yeah. Do you remember some of the bands that played those jobs? Some of the musicians you heard when you were young?

Oh yes. Yes. I remember a lot of those bands. They were old Jack Carey. I forgot to mention Jack my old friend. I did play with Jack Carey a couple of months before he taken sick and died. I played banquets with him. I played banquets with Buddy Petit. I played with Chris Kelly. Also with Kid René. Bill I played most every band in the city. Knowing band in the city. I really did. Played most every knowing band in the city. And good band.
Who were some of your favorite guitar and banjo players? Aside from your brother we know you must have thought John especially was wonderful everyone says.

items.title: Alcide "Slow Drag" Pavageau and Lawrence Marrero Interview, 1957-09-01
items.q: And he played with Kid Rene and Buddy Pitty.

ctx.x: Played with Solishtan a long time. John Marrera. With P. Ron too, didn't he? Yeah. He played with King Joe Oliver. You remember Joe Oliver? Yeah we had the records.

Yeah. And he played with Kid Rene and Buddy Pitty. And he started you on banjo. He started me on banjo. How I started banjo I picked it up to see my mother, she played guitar. My father was a bass player, which you heard about your knowledge. My brother was a bass player and my brother John was a guitar and a banjo player. But they all really was good and I used to listen to them all the time. And my first instrument was a guitar. My first number was Under the Double Eagle. I remember that and I can't play it…
space. space. Two little strings, second, third space, Littlefinger and the one, two, three, four, fifth.

items.title: Lawrence Marrero Interview, 1959-01-02
items.q: I see many times we'd meet on the corner. Buddy Petit, Kid Rene, and Chris Kelly.

ctx.x: Just another minute or two on here, some of the bands that you played with you mentioned all these great trumpet players like Buddy Petit and Chris Kelly and Kid Rene, who was your favorite trumpet player in those days? Or Cornette, whatever they played.

Well uh, what was Cornette, that time Bill, Rene was the most jazzed man we had. I mean for fingering his corner and making those notes. And Sam Morgan was one of the sweetest trumpet players we had. But Chris Kelly, he had the ragged, ragged music you know, all the ragged music that people liked. The low class of people you know. Well he was king of that. I see many times we'd meet on the corner. Buddy Petit, Kid Rene, and Chris Kelly. We'd meet also Punch. Butch Miller, he was here, could tell you the same…

And they get there, at that time they didn't have trouble, they had news and where. They get together, they stay there. Stay there and play, watch Chiron Manila. Rene used to give a sign to go ahead, because Rene and Chris Keller's good friends, you see, he'd give Chris Keller a sign to go ahead and leave him to it. Chris would pull off, you see. And just leave Rene to handle that fella, because Rene could handle him. There was too much for Chris. We had a wonderful time, Bill. Show us some time whenever I was…
